headline: London Director Draws Suspended Sentence and 100 Hours Unpaid Work After £1.1 Million Passes Through Firm With Zero Books
deck: Southwark Crown Court handed former Hope & Pride Limited sole director Jenna Lennon six months suspended for a year after missing accounting records left liquidators unable to verify £1.1 million in inflows or a £396,630 HMRC director’s loan.

financials.fine_display: £0 Criminal Fine (100 Hrs Unpaid Work + 7-Yr Ban)
financials.prison_display: 0 Days Immediate Custody (6 Mos Suspended 12 Mos)

score_provenance.rationale: After pleading guilty to withholding books that left liquidators unable to verify over £1.1 million in bank inflows and a £396,630 HMRC director's loan claim, Jenna Lennon received £0 in criminal fines and zero days of immediate custody under a six-month suspended sentence, offset only by a seven-year directorship ban and 100 hours of unpaid work.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: Former Hope & Pride Limited sole director Jenna Lennon pleaded guilty under the Insolvency Act 1986 after failing to hand over accounting records covering over £1.1 million (~$1.39M) in bank inflows and a £396,630 HMRC director’s loan claim, receiving a six-month suspended sentence, 100 hours of unpaid work, and £0 in criminal fines.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Losing every single receipt for £1.1 million in cash deposits—including nearly £400,000 paid to yourself—and walking out of Crown Court with 100 hours of community service
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Immediate custodial sentences are routine in Crown Court fraud and theft cases involving seven-figure sums, versus zero days behind bars here

sources.title: Company director sentenced after liquidators unable to verify more than £1 million

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Royal Exchange in the City of London. At Southwark Crown Court, former Hope & Pride Limited sole director Jenna Lennon received a six-month suspended sentence and 100 hours of unpaid work after withholding accounting records covering over £1.1 million in bank inflows.
